scope_reference_policy: Official 2025 MD Standards Statement column, not the legacy 2010 previous-standards column; each parent includes any lettered requirements listed. Original wording resides in official linked PDF; editorial scope_summary in inventory is not accepted source-fidelity proof.

records.scope_summary_editorial: Divide fractions by fractions in context, extending estimation, concrete/visual fraction models, and equations.
Fluently divide multi-digit numbers, choosing efficient strategies or the standard algorithm.
Fluently multiply and divide multi-digit decimals to the thousandths in context.
Identify the common factors and multiples of two whole numbers.
Use understanding of rational numbers as positive and negative numbers to describe quantities with opposite directions or values.
Represent rational numbers as points on vertical or horizontal number lines, including points with negative coordinates.
Use perpendicular number lines intersecting at (0,0) to introduce the four quadrants of the Coordinate Plane and represent points with positive and negative coordinates.
Order rational numbers and identify absolute value.
Solve problems in context by graphing points with a shared coordinate in all four quadrants of the Coordinate Plane.
Use ratio language in context to describe a ratio relationship between two quantities, including part-to-part and part-to-whole.
Represent and use unit rates, written as fractions with whole number numerators and denominators, in context.
Use ratio and rate reasoning to solve problems in context with tables of equivalent ratios, tape diagrams, double number lines, or the Coordinate Plane.
Find a percent of a quantity in context as a rate per 100, including finding the whole given a part and the percent, using tables, tape diagrams, and double number lines.
Write numerical expressions involving whole number exponents and positive rational number bases; evaluate with technology.
Write, read, and evaluate expressions in which letters stand for numbers.
Apply properties of operations to generate equivalent algebraic expressions and to identify when two expressions are equivalent.
Solve problems in context by writing and solving equations and interpreting the solutions in context.
Write an inequality of the form x > c or x < c to represent a constraint in context; recognize infinitely many solutions and represent them on number lines.
Solve problems in context by writing and solving inequalities and interpreting solution sets in context.
Use variables to represent two quantities in context that change in relationship to one another.
Find the area of triangles, quadrilaterals, and polygons by composing into rectangles or decomposing into triangles and quadrilaterals.
Find the volume of a right rectangular prism with fractional edge lengths.
Draw polygons in the Coordinate Plane given vertex coordinates and use coordinates to find side lengths; apply these techniques in context.
Represent three-dimensional figures using nets of rectangles and triangles and use the nets to find surface area to solve problems.
Recognize a statistical question as one that anticipates variability in the data related to the question and accounts for it in the answers.
Use the language of probability to describe the likelihood of possible outcomes and to anticipate variability in data collected from statistical questions.
Explain how a data set collected to answer a statistical question has a distribution described by center, spread, and overall shape.
Recognize that a measure of center summarizes all values with a single number while a measure of variation describes how values vary.
Interpret numerical data in plots on a number line, including line plots, histograms, and box plots.
Summarize numerical data sets in relation to their context.
Add and subtract rational numbers using multiple strategies and representations.
Multiply and divide rational numbers using multiple strategies and representations.
Solve multistep problems involving positive and negative rational numbers in any form using all four operations.
Compute unit rates associated with ratios of fractions, including ratios of lengths, areas, and other quantities in like or different units.
Identify proportional relationships between quantities.
Represent proportional relationships between quantities.
Solve ratio and percent problems in context (simple interest, tax, markups/markdowns, tips, commissions, percent change, percent error) by applying proportional reasoning.
Apply properties of operations as strategies to add, subtract, factor, and expand linear expressions with rational coefficients.
Rewrite an expression in different forms to shed light on the represented context and how quantities in it are related.
Analyze contextual situations to determine whether an equation or inequality best represents the relationship between quantities; justify the choice. (New standard.)
Use variables to represent quantities and write and solve equations to model and reason about relationships in context.
Use variables to represent quantities and write and solve inequalities to model and reason about constraints and conditions in context.
Solve problems involving scale drawings of geometric figures, including computing actual lengths and areas and reproducing a drawing at a different scale.
Describe the two-dimensional figures that result from slicing three-dimensional figures with a plane and connect the resulting shapes to the solid's structure.
Apply the formulas for area and circumference of a circle to solve problems in context, using informal reasoning to relate circumference and area.
Solve problems with and without context involving area, surface area, and volume of two- and three-dimensional objects.
Determine when generalizations about a population are appropriate based on how the sample was selected.
Use data from random samples to make and evaluate estimates or predictions about a population.
Compare two numerical data distributions using visual displays and numerical measures to draw inferences about populations.
Explain probability on the 0-1 scale (impossible to certain) and use it to estimate the probability of chance events.
Understand and apply long-run relative frequency to approximate probabilities and make predictions about chance events.
Develop and use probability models to find probabilities of events and compare them to observed results.
Identify a number as irrational when its decimal expansion neither terminates nor repeats; explain that irrational numbers are not a ratio of two integers.
Use rational approximations of irrational numbers to estimate locations on a number line, compare size, and estimate expressions in context.
Know and apply the properties of integer exponents to generate equivalent numerical expressions.
Use square and cube roots to represent solutions to equations and describe numbers.
Apply scientific notation to represent and compare very large and very small quantities in context, and use technology to compute with numbers in scientific notation.
Analyze and compare proportional relationships using slope.
Use proportional reasoning to identify slope and represent linear relationships.
Solve linear equations in one variable.
Solve linear inequalities in one variable.
Analyze and solve systems of two linear equations in two variables.
Determine whether a relationship is a function by analyzing whether each input is assigned to exactly one output.
Compare the properties (rate of change, intercepts) of two linear functions each represented in a different way.
Identify whether a function is linear or non-linear given equations, graphs, or input-output pairs, and justify using constant rate of change.
Interpret the graph of a linear function in the form y = mx + b, identifying slope and y-intercept and matching equations to graphs. (New standard.)
Construct and interpret a linear function to model a relationship between two quantities.
Describe qualitatively the functional relationship between two quantities by analyzing a graph; sketch a graph exhibiting qualitative features.
Use relationships between supplementary, complementary, vertical, and adjacent angles to write and solve equations for an unknown angle.
Draw or build triangles given three measures of angles or sides and determine whether the conditions produce a unique triangle, more than one, or none.
Use informal arguments to verify that the sum of interior angles of a triangle is 180 degrees and the exterior-angle relationship.
Understand and reason about the Pythagorean Theorem and its extensions.
Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to solve problems in context.
Evaluate predictions and conclusions drawn from bivariate data.
Construct and interpret scatter plots for bivariate measurement data to investigate patterns of association.
Compare the fit of different linear models on scatter plots of the same data by describing the overall pattern and closeness of points.
Use a provided linear model to make predictions based on bivariate data and interpret slope and y-intercept in context.
Construct a two-way table for two categorical variables; calculate and interpret relative frequencies to describe possible associations.
Find probabilities of compound events by representing or simulating the sample space or simulating events.
